name: Anthracene Violet
lede: Anthracene Violet is a dark, dusky violet from Ridgway's 1912 chart, rare enough in our archive to appear in only eleven paintings.

sections.title: A rare dusky violet
sections.body: Ridgway's 1912 plate XXV gives this color the name Anthracene Violet, hue 61′, tone k, and the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 files a close match in its block 211 [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[imperial-purple]], [[madder-violet]], [[dusty-purple-tone]] and [[mulberry-purple]], at 2.6, 2.9, 6, 2.9, 3.4 and 4.3 ΔE [1]. The library's closest recorded neighbor is [[imperial-purple]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match to Anthracene Violet in only 11 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed [2]. The earliest dated match is Filippo Lippi's Coronation of the Virgin, from 1441, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. With so few matches, the data cannot support a reliable peak decade or painter; inside a painting it most often sits in shadow, in 64 percent of its appearances [2].
